subject: Oakridge order form — publicity & confidentiality redlines
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oakridge.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: legal@oakridge.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Oakridge order form — publicity & logo usage

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — Oakridge is excited to move forward. Our procurement team attached an updated order form (v2) that includes a short publicity clause and a request for a small logo use for the customer page. Legal asked I loop in your team to confirm Redwood is comfortable with the proposed language.

Key items from our side:
- Standard publicity permission: Oakridge may (at its option) include Redwood in customer lists and a one-paragraph case study quote.
- Logo: small logo on Oakridge customer roster page and in a press deck; Oakridge will follow Redwood logo guidelines.
- Timing: Oakridge plans to announce progress on a product update in mid-December and would like any publicity approval completed by Dec 5.

I attached the order form and our brand guidelines. If Redwood needs edits, please send redlines and we can iterate.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Oakridge Technologies

Attachments: Oakridge_OrderForm_v2.pdf, Oakridge_Brand_Guidelines.pdf

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oakridge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Oakridge order form — publicity & logo usage

Samantha —

Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and David (ops/security) to review. Quick note from product: the one-paragraph quote is fine but we usually require a short approval window on the final text and for logo usage we prefer a published attribution style rather than a locked asset.

Kimberly/David — can you review the attached order form and the brand guidelines and share any redlines by end of day Friday (Nov 21)? Oakridge would like a Dec 5 approval window.

I'll try to keep the back-and-forth minimal — our typical asks:
- Narrow publicity clause to case-study opt-in (no automatic press releases).
- Approval rights on final quote (48 hours).
- Logo usage limited to non-commercial customer roster and press decks; no sublicensing.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Oakridge_OrderForm_v2.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Oakridge order form — publicity & logo usage

Rohan —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Oakridge's proposed publicity and confidentiality language and attached a redline. High-level notes:

1) Publicity: Oakridge's draft is broader than we accept. Proposed edits:
   - Convert to "Oakridge may request permission to use Redwood's name and logo for case study and customer lists. Redwood's prior written consent (which will not be unreasonably withheld) is required for press releases or public announcement text."
   - Add explicit approval window of 48 hours for quotes and 5 business days for press materials.

2) Logo use:
   - Limit to "logo for use on Oakridge's customer roster page and in press decks announcing the joint customer relationship," with a prohibition on redistribution or resale.
   - Require compliance with attached Logo_Guidelines.pdf and delivery of a mock prior to publication.

3) Confidentiality carveout:
   - Add language that prohibits disclosure of confidential product roadmaps, usage metrics or billing amounts in any public materials without prior written consent.

4) Evidence:
   - Oakridge must provide the final copied text and asset mock-ups via the DocuSign/drive link for approval.

I've attached Oakridge_MSA_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx and a short suggested case-study outline. If Oakridge Legal insists on removing the consent requirement entirely, we'll need an exec escalation.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Oakridge_MSA_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx, draft-case-study-outline.docx

From: Oakridge Legal <legal@oakridge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oakridge.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Oakridge order form — publicity & logo usage

Kimberly —

Thanks for the detailed notes. A couple of clarifications from Oakridge Legal:

- Oakridge cannot agree to a total prohibition on mentioning product usage or anonymized metrics in press materials, as our marketing team relies on high-level performance statements. We are open to redaction for sensitive items (no raw usage or billing numbers).
- We are willing to accept a 72-hour approval window for quotes and up to 7 days for full press releases.
- For the logo, we prefer a perpetual non-exclusive license for the purposes outlined (customer page + press decks).

We're attaching an alternative short redline (see attached) that keeps Oakridge's needed flexibility for marketing. If Redwood requires the checkbox to be explicit for each case study, we'll need a short operational flow to handle approvals.

Regards,
Eleanor Park
Corporate Counsel
Oakridge Technologies

Attachments: Oakridge_legal_redline_v2.docx

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oakridge.com>, Eleanor Park <legal@oakridge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 09:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Oakridge order form — publicity & logo usage

Eleanor/Samantha —

Appreciate the flexibility. We're close on scope. Proposed compromise actionable items:

1) Approval windows: 72 hours for paragraph quotes; 7 business days for press releases (agreed).
2) Logo license: perpetual, non-exclusive for the two use cases, but Oakridge must supply a mock and include Redwood's brand guidelines link and a required attribution line. No sublicensing or sale.
3) Confidentiality: Oakridge may include high-level anonymized performance metrics (e.g., "reduced inference latency by >30%"), but anything that reveals billing, raw usage counts, or roadmap specifics requires prior consent.

Operational flow:
- Oakridge sends a request via the shared Drive link with the mock and final copy.
- Redwood has 72 hours to respond to paragraph quotes; 7 business days for releases. Silence = explicit approval for quotes only.

Marissa (Marketing) — can you own the operational flow and approve brand assets?

If that works we can update the order form and proceed to signature.

Thanks,
Rohan
